scope: Generated fixture, browser validation, prompt-pack pressure, and representative visual inspection only. This is not saved-site validation and not a conformance publication lane.

wcag.interpretation: Barrier-side packets require same-process evidence, same information previously provided, required re-entry, and no auto-populate/selection/exception evidence. Control packets expose exception or non-applicability evidence and must resolve to UNCERTAIN, not a pass.

fixtureValidation.result: 120/120 pass; redundant-entry 10/10 positive and 10/10 negative controls observed as expected

browserProbeTests.result: 35/35 pass; includes real runBroadScopeForUrl claim-propagation assertion and postal-code non-auth regression

packetValidation.result: redundant-entry 20 packets; 10 LIKELY_BARRIER positives, 10 UNCERTAIN controls; 0 converted judgments

inspected.finding: Visible text asks for email again and states it was entered on the previous step.
Visible control shows the repeated email value reused automatically.
Visible control provides a user-confirmed reuse mechanism: Use same as shipping.

remediationsFromThisPass: Generated redundant-entry fixtures now cover ten barrier variants and ten control/exception variants.
The collector emits SC 3.3.7 predicate claims instead of relying on duplicate field names alone.
Prompt rules allow only LIKELY_BARRIER or UNCERTAIN and explicitly encode auto-populate, selection, optional, security, invalid-data, and essential exceptions.
Prompt-pack, packet-validation, and pressure scripts now emit redundant-entry control packets instead of silently routing them to NO_REVIEW.
The auth detector no longer treats generic postal code fields as authentication code fields.
The real runBroadScopeForUrl path now preserves evidenceClaims/evidenceStrength from non-interference, interaction, authentication, and redundant-entry candidates.

Broad-scope review now clamps judge outputs to per-aspect allowedVerdicts, so redundant-entry/media/auth sidecar packets cannot retain a disallowed LIKELY_OK even if an injected judge and critic agree.

independentReview.summary: Independent review accepted the generated 10/10 fixture semantics as controls, but found three issues: real runBroadScopeForUrl dropped evidence claims, sidecar review did not hard-clamp disallowed LIKELY_OK verdicts, and fixture metadata is not real process proof. The first two were fixed and regression-tested; the third remains an explicit scope limitation.
remainingReviewerCaveats: Generated data-v3 attributes are valid fixture controls but not Trusted Tester-style real process evidence unless backed by prior-step traces, manifests, saved values, or observed reuse mechanisms.
EN 301 549 references for SC 3.3.7 should be treated as future/applicable-WCAG pass-through context, not as an independent EN 301 549 V3.2.1 clause.

remainingLimits: The lane still uses generated fixture metadata for same-process and previously-provided facts; real saved sites need process/session traces or manifests.
The lane does not prove complete process conformance.
Exception adequacy remains semantic and process-scoped.
Absence of a redundant-entry packet must never be read as a pass.
